chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad and Ahmad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father from Abdillah ibn Bukayr from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is recommended for the fasting person, if he is able to do so, to pray before breaking his fast.

key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: Recommended (a legal ruling less obligatory than wajib but more than mubah)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended action for a fasting person before breaking their fast according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the spiritual merit of offering voluntary prayers, such as Salat al-Fajr or Du'a al-Iftar, before consuming food, provided one retains sufficient strength. This practice underscores the principle that fasting is not merely physical abstinence but a holistic state of worship where the believer seeks closeness to Allah through additional acts of devotion at the moment of breaking the fast. It reflects the scholarly view that maintaining spiritual alertness during Iftar enhances the reward of the fast.
